your_life.name: Inspector Arun Mehra
your_life.recollections:
Before the district office, before the uniform, there was Mill Lane: the rasp of your father's wheel plane through the open workshop door and Tara making you wait while she tied her shoes. You left Bhairav's Hollow with a habit of looking back at the chapel turn. Twelve winters have passed since Mercy House sent the letter saying your sister had died of fever. Requests for the original papers have filled a drawer in your room at headquarters; the paper has aged more visibly than the answers have changed.

Leena used to know where you kept that drawer. You lived together for three years, separated, and learned to write letters about the practical things that remained. Her mother once set tea in front of you after Tara's funeral. Raghav's signature is familiar from replies to your requests. None of those memories tells you what happened this evening.

Kabir has worked beside you for six years. You remember the floodwater in the cellar where you pulled him out, but also uneventful journeys, poor meals and the little habits by which colleagues become familiar. Dr. Mira Sen's invitation brought you back on leave: she wanted to discuss an old family record. No death had been reported when you set out. Now the coach journey is behind you, the town is under snow, and you have reached Mercy House.

place.name: Mercy House archive
place.description: The lamps have been turned up too high. Above their yellow circles the archive disappears into beams and soot, and each time the wind presses against the casement the flames lean together. A desk stands under the window, its blotter crowded by ordinary papers. Beyond it are shelves, a cold fireplace and a service door whose lower edge has worn a pale arc into the boards. From the scullery comes the intermittent complaint of a kettle. Nothing in the room tells you how much of this evening anyone outside it could have seen.

place.name: Mercy House courtyard
place.description: Snow collects along the courtyard walls without yet settling in the wheel ruts. A gate lamp turns the falling flakes into brief bright scratches. Behind you Mercy House has too many dark windows; ahead, the road drops toward the square. A narrower way runs beside the wall to Dev's winter garden. The distances are short enough for a cry to carry, although a cry alone would explain very little.

place.name: Dev’s house and winter garden
place.description: Dev's house shelters behind winter beds edged with salvaged slate. Snow has softened most of the garden into one surface, broken by the tool shed and the kitchen table visible under a lean-to. Somewhere under the beds are last month's bulbs; from where you stand you cannot tell whether anything more recent lies beneath them. A path follows the fence toward the cemetery, while the courtyard lamp remains visible behind you.

findings.label: disturbed soil
findings.description: The soil above last month’s bulbs has recently been lifted. The depression is longer than a garden trench.

findings.label: spade
findings.description: A working spade with a broad iron blade and fresh soil on its edge.

place.name: Old cemetery
place.description: The oldest stones lean in different directions, as though the ground has shifted separately beneath each family. Beyond the named graves, fir needles lie over smaller unmarked mounds. The burial office is shut against the weather. Paths lead to the chapel, the winter garden and the forest edge. Standing among graves does not establish when a body arrived, who brought it or why.

place.name: Chapel
place.description: The chapel has kept the day's cold. A few candles burn near the inner door, too small to warm the stone, and a register lies on the keeper's side desk. Pews make quiet islands of darkness beneath the windows. People sometimes come here because they want witnesses, and sometimes because they do not. The square is behind the outer door; a side path crosses to the cemetery.

findings.label: parish register
findings.description: The original parish register includes Nera among the ninth ward deaths twelve winters ago. Dates and entry numbers are legible beneath the keeper’s old certification.

place.name: Town square
place.description: The square has emptied before the shops have quite closed. Shutters answer one another across the road, and a horse drinks noisily at the trough beneath the notice board. The Pine Lantern keeps a strip of light under its door. Paths lead toward the chapel, the Das and Rao households, and the Mercy House courtyard; beyond the last lamp the forest road becomes a different shade of black. You remember this crossing from childhood, though the signs above the shops have changed.

place.name: Rao household
place.description: The threshold has been lowered and the study furniture set far apart, leaving a clear passage for a wheelchair. On the workbench, acoustic drawings lie under smooth stones. A correspondence drawer sits closed beneath them. From the courtyard comes the click of a loose gate fastening; the street beyond returns to the square. An arrangement made for someone's convenience tells you nothing, by itself, about their conduct tonight.
